## Varied {#chords-auto}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Varied**. It is built up from 3 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The band chooses: two-bar phrases built from the swing figures, with some bars left empty. In straight eighths it plays the boogaloo stabs. Tick rhythms under it and it varies between just those.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Varied","opts":{"compRhythm":"auto"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Charleston

Start with something simpler. A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-charleston) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Reverse Charleston

The Charleston displaced: a short chord on the and of 1 and a held one on beat 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-reverse) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Reverse Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"reverse"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Red Garland

Chords on the and of 2 and the and of 4. The second one anticipates the next bar's chord and is held across the barline.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-garland) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Red Garland","opts":{"compRhythm":"garland"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Varied, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Real comping mixes the figures you have learned: two-bar phrases, some bars left empty. Choose one figure per bar and vary it; leave space for the soloist.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Varied","opts":{"compRhythm":"auto"}},{"label":"Red Garland (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"garland"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Varied","opts":{"compRhythm":"auto"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Varied","opts":{"compRhythm":"auto"}}]'></div>

### Step 7: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Varied","opts":{"compRhythm":"auto"}}]'></div>

The same comping rhythm in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Jazz ballad**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Varied","opts":{"compRhythm":"auto"}}]'></div>

## Charleston {#chords-charleston}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Charleston**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

It belongs in *Swing* and *Jazz ballad*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Quarter-note chords

The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Charleston, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A held chord on 1 and a short one on the and of 2 (swung). Say it: ONE ... and. On piano, a rootless voicing in the left hand; on guitar, a three-note shape with the second chord choked.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}},{"label":"Quarter-note chords (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same comping rhythm in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Jazz ballad**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

- **Other comping rhythms in the Jazz group:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto), [Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-charleston), [Reverse Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-reverse), [Off-beats](chords.qmd#chords-offbeats), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad), [Four to the bar](chords.qmd#chords-four), [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs), [Stride](chords.qmd#chords-stride).

## Off-beats {#chords-offbeats}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Off-beats**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Chords on the and of 1 and the and of 3, never on a downbeat.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Charleston

Start with something simpler. A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-charleston) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Reverse Charleston

The Charleston displaced: a short chord on the and of 1 and a held one on beat 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-reverse) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Reverse Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"reverse"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Off-beats, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Chords on the and of 1 and the and of 3, never on a downbeat. Keep them short and light; they float on top of the walking bass.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}},{"label":"Reverse Charleston (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"reverse"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-charleston), [Reverse Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-reverse).
- **Leads to:** [Red Garland](chords.qmd#chords-garland), [So What: the answer](chords.qmd#chords-sowhat): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Walking](bass.qmd#bass-walk) (bass line), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Jazz group:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto), [Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-charleston), [Reverse Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-reverse), [Red Garland](chords.qmd#chords-garland), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad), [Four to the bar](chords.qmd#chords-four), [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs), [Stride](chords.qmd#chords-stride).

## Long notes {#chords-pad}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Long notes**. It is one of the first patterns to learn, so this page starts from it and takes it into the band. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad*, *Boogaloo*, *Bossa nova*, *Tango*, *Piano ballad*, *Boom-chick*, *Straight-eighth rock*, *Reggaeton*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop*, *12/8 doo-wop*, *Hymn (four parts)*, *Folk carol*, *Emo / pop-punk* and *John Prine Fingerpicking*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes, slowly

**How to play it.** One chord, struck once, held for the bar. On piano, play it and keep the keys down (or the pedal down) until the chord changes; on guitar, strum once and let it ring. Use it to learn the chords and the changes before any rhythm.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 72 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C G|Am F|Dm G|C" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

The same comping rhythm in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

## Four to the bar {#chords-four}

*For guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Four to the bar**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A short chord on every beat with 2 and 4 a little louder, the way Freddie Green played rhythm guitar.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Boogie-woogie* and *Jump blues*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four to the bar","opts":{"compRhythm":"four"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Quarter-note chords

The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Four to the bar, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A short chord on every beat, 2 and 4 a little louder, the way Freddie Green played. On guitar use three-note shapes on the middle strings and release the pressure right after each strum.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four to the bar","opts":{"compRhythm":"four"}},{"label":"Quarter-note chords (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four to the bar","opts":{"compRhythm":"four"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four to the bar","opts":{"compRhythm":"four"}}]'></div>

The same comping rhythm in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Stride**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The stride pianist's left hand: a low bass note on beats 1 and 3 (the root in octaves where a chord starts, its fifth on beat 3) and the chord in the middle of the keyboard on beats 2 and 4. In 3/4 the bass on 1 and the chord on 2 and 3. On the guitar it is plain boom-chick.

It belongs in *Stride piano* and *Ragtime*. Here it is in the stride piano style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah

Start with something simpler. Short chords on the beats the bass leaves free: 2 and 4 in 4/4, 2 and 3 in a waltz. Goes with the Root and fifth bass line.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-oompah) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Stride, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The left hand alone first: a low octave on the root on beat 1, a chord about two octaves higher on beat 2, the fifth down low on beat 3, the chord again on 4. Look at where the hand lands, not where it has been: the leap down is the hard one. Keep the bass notes short and the chords lighter. When it is steady, let the band's bass and drums join.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}},{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C A7|Dm7 G7|C C7|F G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a jazz waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same comping rhythm in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Ragtime**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ragtime" data-chart="C|C|G7|C" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords.qmd#chords-oompah).
- **Leads to:** [Stride in tenths](chords.qmd#chords-stride-tenths): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords.qmd#chords-oompah) (comping rhythm), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two) (bass line), [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt) (bass line).
- **Plays with, in stride piano:** [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two) (bass line), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Jazz group:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto), [Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-charleston), [Reverse Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-reverse), [Red Garland](chords.qmd#chords-garland), [Off-beats](chords.qmd#chords-offbeats), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad), [Four to the bar](chords.qmd#chords-four), [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs).

## Stride in tenths {#chords-stride-tenths}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Stride in tenths**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Stride with a wider left hand: on beat 1 a tenth (the root with the chord's 3rd an octave above it, together); on beat 3 the fifth, or, when the chord is about to change, a tenth walking to a step from the next root. Chords in the middle of the keyboard on 2 and 4. A tenth that would crowd the chords is played as its low note alone. On the guitar it is plain boom-chick.

It belongs in *Stride piano* and *Ragtime*. Here it is in the stride piano style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride in tenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strideTenths"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah

Start with something simpler. Short chords on the beats the bass leaves free: 2 and 4 in 4/4, 2 and 3 in a waltz. Goes with the Root and fifth bass line.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-oompah) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Stride

The stride pianist's left hand: a low bass note on beats 1 and 3 (the root in octaves where a chord starts, its fifth on beat 3) and the chord in the middle of the keyboard on beats 2 and 4. In 3/4 the bass on 1 and the chord on 2 and 3. On the guitar it is plain boom-chick.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-stride) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Stride in tenths, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The stride left hand, stretched: on beat 1 the root with the 3rd an octave above it, both at once (roll them if your hand will not reach). On beat 3 the fifth, or, before a chord change, a tenth a step away from the next root, so the bass walks into it. Learn the leaps first with single notes, then add the top of each tenth.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride in tenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strideTenths"}},{"label":"Stride (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"stride"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride in tenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strideTenths"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C A7|Dm7 G7|C C7|F G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride in tenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strideTenths"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same comping rhythm in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Ragtime**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ragtime" data-chart="C|C|G7|C" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Stride in tenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strideTenths"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords.qmd#chords-oompah), [Stride](chords.qmd#chords-stride).
- **Plays with, in stride piano:** [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two) (bass line), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Jazz group:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto), [Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-charleston), [Reverse Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-reverse), [Red Garland](chords.qmd#chords-garland), [Off-beats](chords.qmd#chords-offbeats), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad), [Four to the bar](chords.qmd#chords-four), [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs).

## Boogie-woogie right hand {#chords-boogie}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Boogie-woogie right hand**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar riff of short swung chords against the walking left hand: beat 1, the and of 1 and the and of 2 (held); then the and of 1, beat 2 and the and of 3 (held).

It belongs in *Boogie-woogie* and *Jump blues*. Here it is in the boogie-woogie style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Every off-beat

Start with something simpler. A short chord on the and of every beat and never on the beat: the ska and calypso afterbeat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-upbeats) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Charleston

A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-charleston) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Boogie-woogie right hand, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Short chords against the walking bass, a two-bar riff: 1, the and of 1, the and of 2 held; then the and of 1, 2, the and of 3 held. Keep the right hand light and swung, and play the same riff on every chord of the blues: it does not need to change, the bass does the moving.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}},{"label":"Charleston (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|F7 F#dim7|C7|G7 F7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same comping rhythm in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Jump blues**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="jump" data-chart="C7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="160" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Every off-beat](chords.qmd#chords-upbeats), [Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-charleston).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Boogie-woogie](bass.qmd#bass-boogie) (bass line), [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass.qmd#bass-arp) (bass line), [Blues shuffle](drums.qmd#drums-shuffle) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in boogie-woogie:** [Boogie-woogie](bass.qmd#bass-boogie) (bass line), [Blues shuffle](drums.qmd#drums-shuffle) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Jazz group:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto), [Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-charleston), [Reverse Charleston](chords.qmd#chords-reverse), [Red Garland](chords.qmd#chords-garland), [Off-beats](chords.qmd#chords-offbeats), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad), [Four to the bar](chords.qmd#chords-four), [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs).

## So What: the answer {#chords-sowhat}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **So What: the answer**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar pattern. Nothing in the first bar, under the bass call. In the second, two chords: the voicing a whole step above the chord, held from beat 3, then the chord itself, short, on the and of 4. Use the Fourths voicing for the sound of the record.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Off-beats

Chords on the and of 1 and the and of 3, never on a downbeat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-offbeats) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: So What: the answer, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars: nothing in the first while the bass plays the call; in the second, a chord a whole step above held from 3, then the chord itself, short, on the and of 4. 'So what.'

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}},{"label":"Off-beats (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the answer","opts":{"compRhythm":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad), [Off-beats](chords.qmd#chords-offbeats).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [So What: the bass call](bass.qmd#bass-sowhat) (bass line).
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Walking](bass.qmd#bass-walk) (bass line), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the From tunes group:** [Maiden Voyage](chords.qmd#chords-maiden), [Take Five vamp](chords.qmd#chords-takefive).

## Maiden Voyage {#chords-maiden}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Maiden Voyage**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar pattern of held chords: 1, the and of 2 and 4 (held over the barline), then the and of 2 and 4.

It belongs in *Boogaloo* and *Bossa nova*. Here it is in the bossa nova style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Maiden Voyage","opts":{"compRhythm":"maiden"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: 3+3+2 (tresillo)

Three held chords in a bar of eight eighth notes, grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Clocks, Shape of You, Eye of the Tiger.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

### Step 3: Maiden Voyage, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars of held chords: 1, the and of 2 and 4 (held over the barline), then the and of 2 and 4. The bass plays the same rhythm: play together.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Maiden Voyage","opts":{"compRhythm":"maiden"}},{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo) (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

The same comping rhythm in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

## Take Five vamp {#chords-takefive}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Take Five vamp**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

For 5/4, grouped 3 + 2: a held chord on 1, a short one on the and of 2, then short chords on 4 and 5.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-charleston) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

**How to play it.** 5/4 grouped 3+2: held chord on 1, short on the and of 2, short chords on 4 and 5. It is the Charleston with two more beats.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

## Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah {#chords-oompah}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Short chords on the beats the bass leaves free: 2 and 4 in 4/4, 2 and 3 in a waltz. Goes with the Root and fifth bass line.

It belongs in *Boom-chick*, *Country train beat*, *Motown / soul*, *Folk carol*, *Stride piano* and *Ragtime*. Here it is in the boom-chick style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Short chords on 2 and 4 where the bass leaves room (on 2 and 3 in a waltz). On piano: left hand plays the bass on 1 and 3, right hand the chord on 2 and 4. On guitar: pick the bass note, then strum the chord.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

## Waltz in one {#chords-waltz}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Waltz in one**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

For a quick 3/4. The root on 1 and light, short chords on 2 and 3, the third beat the lighter. The bars go in fours: the first leans, the third a little, and the fourth grows into the next phrase. In 4/4 it is boom-chick.

It belongs in *Waltz (in one)*, *Boom-chick*, *Folk carol* and *Hymn (four parts)*. Here it is in the waltz (in one) style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Ballad: rocking {#chords-ball-rock}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Ballad: rocking**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Quarter notes: the chord on 1, the thumb on 2, the top two notes on 3, the thumb on 4, over held left-hand octaves on the root. On the piano with the Standard voicing the chord is a triad in first inversion.

It belongs in *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Folk carol*, *Hymn (four parts)* and *12/8 doo-wop*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: rocking","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballRock"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Hymn: four parts

Every chord played once and held until the next one. On the piano or organ it is four parts: the root in the left hand and three voices above it that move as little as possible from chord to chord. It follows the chart's chords, so a carol written with a chord on every beat sounds like the hymnal.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-hymn) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Ballad: rocking, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Left hand: an octave on the root, held. Right hand in quarter notes: the whole chord on 1, the thumb on 2, the top two notes on 3, the thumb on 4. The right hand rocks between the thumb and the top.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: rocking","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballRock"}},{"label":"Hymn: four parts (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

## Ballad: half-broken {#chords-ball-broken}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Ballad: half-broken**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar pattern. Three notes up the chord (thumb, middle, top) and the whole chord held from beat 3; then the chord held from beat 1 and the three notes on beats 3 and 4.

It belongs in *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Folk carol* and *Hymn (four parts)*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: half-broken","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballBroken"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Ballad: rocking

Start with something simpler. Quarter notes: the chord on 1, the thumb on 2, the top two notes on 3, the thumb on 4, over held left-hand octaves on the root. On the piano with the Standard voicing the chord is a triad in first inversion.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-ball-rock) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: rocking","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballRock"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Arpeggio, up and down

The notes of the voicing one at a time in eighth notes, up to the top and back down, each left to ring.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-arp) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Ballad: half-broken, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars. Bar one: three notes up the chord (thumb, middle, top), then the whole chord held from beat 3. Bar two: the chord held from 1, then the three notes on 3 and 4. Over held left-hand octaves.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: half-broken","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballBroken"}},{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 72 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

## Ballad: syncopated {#chords-ball-sync}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Ballad: syncopated**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Three held sounds a bar: the chord on beat 1, its top two notes on the and of 2 and on beat 4 (3+3+2).

It belongs in *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum* and *Folk carol*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: syncopated","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballSync"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: 3+3+2 (tresillo)

Three held chords in a bar of eight eighth notes, grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Clocks, Shape of You, Eye of the Tiger.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Ballad: syncopated, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Three sounds a bar grouped 3+3+2: the chord on 1, its top two notes on the and of 2 and on 4. Hold each one until the next. The left hand stays on the root octave.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: syncopated","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballSync"}},{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo) (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 72 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: syncopated","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballSync"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C G|Am F|Dm G|C" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: syncopated","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballSync"}}]'></div>

## Quarter-note chords {#chords-quarters}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Quarter-note chords**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

It belongs in *Piano ballad*, *Straight-eighth rock*, *Acoustic strum*, *Motown / soul*, *Hymn (four parts)*, *Folk carol* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Quarter-note chords, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The chord on every beat. On piano: right hand plays the chord on each beat, left hand plays the root as the chord arrives. On guitar: four even downstrokes. Keep every chord the same loudness.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}},{"label":"Long notes (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

## Triplet chords (12/8) {#chords-triplets}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Triplet chords (12/8)**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The chord on all three eighth notes of every beat, the doo-wop piano part. In 4/4 they are played as triplets.

It belongs in *12/8 doo-wop*. Here it is in the 12/8 doo-wop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Triplet chords (12/8), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The chord on all three eighths of every beat: 1-and-a, 2-and-a. Right hand, light repeated chords from the wrist; left hand, the root on 1 and 3. Lean slightly on each beat.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}},{"label":"Quarter-note chords (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 66 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C Am|F G|C Am|F G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Quarter-note chords](chords.qmd#chords-quarters).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [12/8 ballad](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8) (bass line), [12/8](drums.qmd#drums-twelve8) (drum groove), [Blues shuffle](drums.qmd#drums-shuffle) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in 12/8 doo-wop:** [12/8 ballad](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8) (bass line), [12/8](drums.qmd#drums-twelve8) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords.qmd#chords-oompah), [Waltz in one](chords.qmd#chords-waltz), [Ballad: rocking](chords.qmd#chords-ball-rock), [Ballad: half-broken](chords.qmd#chords-ball-broken), [Ballad: syncopated](chords.qmd#chords-ball-sync), [Quarter-note chords](chords.qmd#chords-quarters), [Driving eighths](chords.qmd#chords-eighths), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo).

## 3+3+2 (tresillo) {#chords-tresillo}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **3+3+2 (tresillo)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Three held chords in a bar of eight eighth notes, grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Clocks, Shape of You, Eye of the Tiger.

It belongs in *Dance pop*, *Straight-eighth rock* and *Reggaeton*. Here it is in the dance pop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Ballad: syncopated

Three held sounds a bar: the chord on beat 1, its top two notes on the and of 2 and on beat 4 (3+3+2).

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-ball-sync) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ballad: syncopated","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballSync"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: 3+3+2 (tresillo), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Three held chords grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Count eight eighths and play on 1, 4 and 7. Hold each chord until the next.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}},{"label":"Ballad: syncopated (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"ballSync"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

The same comping rhythm in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.
