## The Barbara Ann rhythm {#chords-barbara}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **The Barbara Ann rhythm**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar pattern: 1, 2, 3 and the and of 4 (shown), then the and of 1, the and of 2, and 3. Barbara Ann, You Can't Hurry Love, Walking on Sunshine.

It belongs in *Motown / soul* and *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the motown / soul style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"The Barbara Ann rhythm","opts":{"compRhythm":"barbara"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: 3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat

The chords play the 3-2 son clave over two bars. First bar (shown): 1, the and of 2, 4. Second bar: 2 and 3. Faith, Desire, I Want Candy.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-clave32) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: The Barbara Ann rhythm, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars: 1, 2, 3 and the and of 4; then the and of 1, the and of 2 and 3. The chord on the and of 4 is the push into the second bar. Say it to the words of Barbara Ann.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

## Alberti bass {#chords-alberti}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Alberti bass**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The notes of the chord one at a time in eighth notes: lowest, highest, middle, highest. Mozart's Sonata K. 545.

It belongs in *Piano ballad* and *Boom-chick*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Alberti bass","opts":{"compRhythm":"alberti"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hymn: four parts

Start with something simpler. Every chord played once and held until the next one. On the piano or organ it is four parts: the root in the left hand and three voices above it that move as little as possible from chord to chord. It follows the chart's chords, so a carol written with a chord on every beat sounds like the hymnal.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-hymn) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Arpeggio, low and high

Eighth notes rocking between the lowest and the highest note of the voicing.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-arp2) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, low and high","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp2"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Alberti bass, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Lowest, highest, middle, highest, in even eighths. Keep the chord under the hand and let the fingers do the work: 5-1-3-1 in the left hand, or 1-5-3-5 in the right. Quiet and even, the way Mozart wrote it.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Alberti bass","opts":{"compRhythm":"alberti"}},{"label":"Arpeggio, low and high (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp2"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 72 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Alberti bass","opts":{"compRhythm":"alberti"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C G|Am F|Dm G|C" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Alberti bass","opts":{"compRhythm":"alberti"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

## Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2 {#chords-g333322}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Sixteen eighth notes over two bars grouped 3+3+3+3+2+2. First bar (shown): 1, the and of 2, 4. Second bar: the and of 1, 3, 4. Beautiful Day.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock* and *Dance pop*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2","opts":{"compRhythm":"g333322"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: 3+3+2 (tresillo)

Start with something simpler. Three held chords in a bar of eight eighth notes, grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Clocks, Shape of You, Eye of the Tiger.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

### Step 2: 3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat

The chords play the 3-2 son clave over two bars. First bar (shown): 1, the and of 2, 4. Second bar: 2 and 3. Faith, Desire, I Want Candy.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-clave32) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Sixteen eighths over two bars grouped 3+3+3+3+2+2. Count the groups, not the beats: one-two-three, one-two-three, ... one-two, one-two. Play a chord on the first of each group.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2","opts":{"compRhythm":"g333322"}},{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

## Groups: eight 3s then four 2s (sixteenths) {#chords-g3x8}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Groups: eight 3s then four 2s (sixteenths)**. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

### The pattern

Two bars of sixteenth notes: eight groups of three, then four groups of two to square it up. Ghostbusters, Raise Your Glass. For slow and medium tempos.

It belongs in *Dance pop* and *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the dance pop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: eight 3s then four 2s (sixteenths)","opts":{"compRhythm":"g3x8"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: 3+3+2 (tresillo)

Start with something simpler. Three held chords in a bar of eight eighth notes, grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Clocks, Shape of You, Eye of the Tiger.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

### Step 2: Strum: sixteenths

The D, D-U, U-D-U strum at double speed, twice in the bar. For slow and medium tempos.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-strum16) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: sixteenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strum16"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Groups: eight 3s then four 2s (sixteenths), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Sixteenths in groups of three for a bar and a half, then four groups of two. The accents slide across the beat. Count sixteenths slowly, accent every third, and let the twos square it up.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: eight 3s then four 2s (sixteenths)","opts":{"compRhythm":"g3x8"}},{"label":"Strum: sixteenths (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"strum16"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: eight 3s then four 2s (sixteenths)","opts":{"compRhythm":"g3x8"}}]'></div>

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

## Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U {#chords-strum-camp}

*For guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The strum most songbooks start with: down on 1, down-up on 2, then up, down-up through 3 and 4 (the hand misses the strings on beat 3).

It belongs in *Acoustic strum*, *Straight-eighth rock*, *Boom-chick* and *Folk carol*. Here it is in the acoustic strum style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumCamp"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Strum: downstrokes on the beat

Start with something simpler. One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-strum-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U

Down on 1 and 3, down-up on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-strum-folk) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Down, down-up, (miss) up, down-up. The hand never stops moving down-up in eighths; on beat 3 it moves down without touching the strings. Say it: 1, 2-and, and, 4-and.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumCamp"}},{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumCamp"}}]'></div>

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

## Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus {#chords-strum-punk}

It belongs in *Emo / pop-punk* and *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the emo / pop-punk style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

Start with something simpler. One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-strum-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

### Step 2: Strum: down-up eighths

Every eighth note, down on the beat and up off it, leaning on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-strum-eights) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="emo" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="106" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Verse: palm-muted downstrokes on every eighth, the side of the picking hand resting on the strings by the bridge. Chorus: lift the hand and play open down-up eighths. The change between them is the arrangement.

## Strum: downstrokes on the beat {#chords-strum-quarters}

*For guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: downstrokes on the beat**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

It belongs in *Acoustic strum*, *Straight-eighth rock*, *Boom-chick*, *Piano ballad*, *Folk carol* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the acoustic strum style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Strum: downstrokes on the beat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Four downstrokes a bar, from the wrist, the hand moving down on every beat. Let each strum ring into the next. This is the motion every other strum is built on: the hand keeps going down on the beat.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}},{"label":"Long notes (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

## Strum: 3-3-2 accents {#chords-strum332}

*For guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: 3-3-2 accents**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The D, D-U, U-D-U strum with the weight moved to beat 1, the and of 2 and beat 4, the 3+3+2 grouping under a great many pop songs.

It belongs in *Acoustic strum*, *Straight-eighth rock* and *Dance pop*. Here it is in the acoustic strum style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

### Step 2: Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U

The strum most songbooks start with: down on 1, down-up on 2, then up, down-up through 3 and 4 (the hand misses the strings on beat 3).

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-strum-camp) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

**How to play it.** The same down-up motion, with the weight on beat 1, the and of 2 and beat 4 (3+3+2). Play the accented strums across all the strings and the others lightly on the top strings.

## Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and {#chords-prine}

*For guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Thumb and fingers, after John Prine. The thumb plays every beat on the low strings: the root, an inner string, the alternate bass, the inner string again. The fingers pinch a treble string with the thumb on 2 and 4 and add the string below it on the and after. In 3/4 the pinches are on 2 and 3.

It belongs in *John Prine Fingerpicking*, *Boom-chick*, *Acoustic strum*, *Folk carol* and *Country train beat*. Here it is in the john prine fingerpicking style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and","opts":{"compRhythm":"prine"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Strum: downstrokes on the beat

Start with something simpler. One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-strum-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah

Short chords on the beats the bass leaves free: 2 and 4 in 4/4, 2 and 3 in a waltz. Goes with the Root and fifth bass line.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-oompah) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The thumb plays every beat: root, an inner string, the alternate bass, the inner string. On 2 and 4 a finger pinches a treble string together with the thumb, and on the and after it plays the string below. Get the thumb going alone first; it must not stop when the fingers join.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and","opts":{"compRhythm":"prine"}},{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 100 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and","opts":{"compRhythm":"prine"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

## Fingerpicking: Travis pattern {#chords-travis}

*For guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Fingerpicking: Travis pattern**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The same thumb on every beat: root, inner string, alternate bass, inner string. The fingers pinch with it on beat 1, then play between the thumb's notes: the and of 2, the and of 3, the and of 4.

It belongs in *John Prine Fingerpicking*, *Boom-chick*, *Acoustic strum*, *Folk carol* and *Country train beat*. Here it is in the john prine fingerpicking style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Fingerpicking: Travis pattern","opts":{"compRhythm":"travis"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and

Start with something simpler. Thumb and fingers, after John Prine. The thumb plays every beat on the low strings: the root, an inner string, the alternate bass, the inner string again. The fingers pinch a treble string with the thumb on 2 and 4 and add the string below it on the and after. In 3/4 the pinches are on 2 and 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-prine) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and","opts":{"compRhythm":"prine"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Fingerpicking: Travis pattern, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The same thumb on every beat. The fingers pinch with the thumb on beat 1, then play in between the thumb notes: the and of 2, the and of 3, the and of 4. Thumb and fingers alternate like two players.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Fingerpicking: Travis pattern","opts":{"compRhythm":"travis"}},{"label":"Fingerpicking: thumb, pinch-and (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"prine"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 100 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Fingerpicking: Travis pattern","opts":{"compRhythm":"travis"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

## Arpeggio, up and down {#chords-arp}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Arpeggio, up and down**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The notes of the voicing one at a time in eighth notes, up to the top and back down, each left to ring.

It belongs in *Piano ballad*, *Jazz ballad*, *Boom-chick*, *Acoustic strum*, *12/8 doo-wop*, *Hymn (four parts)* and *Folk carol*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Arpeggio, low and high

Eighth notes rocking between the lowest and the highest note of the voicing.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-arp2) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, low and high","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp2"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Arpeggio, up and down, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The notes of the chord one at a time in eighths, up and back down, each left to ring. Piano: one hand position per chord, using the pedal. Guitar: hold the whole chord shape and pick string by string.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}},{"label":"Arpeggio, low and high (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp2"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 72 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C G|Am F|Dm G|C" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 7: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

## Hymn: four parts {#chords-hymn}

*For piano, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hymn: four parts**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Every chord played once and held until the next one. On the piano or organ it is four parts: the root in the left hand and three voices above it that move as little as possible from chord to chord. It follows the chart's chords, so a carol written with a chord on every beat sounds like the hymnal.

It belongs in *Hymn (four parts)*, *Folk carol* and *Piano ballad*. Here it is in the hymn (four parts) style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="56" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Hymn: four parts, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Four parts: left hand plays the root; right hand plays three notes that move as little as possible to the next chord. Keep any note two chords share in the same finger, and move the others to the nearest note of the new chord.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="56" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}},{"label":"Long notes (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 80 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C F|G C|Am F|G C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same comping rhythm in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Folk carol**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

**Piano ballad**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hymn: four parts","opts":{"compRhythm":"hymn"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad).
- **Leads to:** [Ballad: rocking](chords.qmd#chords-ball-rock), [Alberti bass](chords.qmd#chords-alberti): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Held roots (the bass voice)](bass.qmd#bass-held) (bass line), [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves) (bass line), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad) (comping rhythm), [Light time](drums.qmd#drums-brushes) (drum groove).

## Every off-beat {#chords-upbeats}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Every off-beat**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A short chord on the and of every beat and never on the beat: the ska and calypso afterbeat.

It belongs in *Calypso*, *Ska / reggae*, *Freylekhs / polka* and *Boogie-woogie*. Here it is in the ska / reggae style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggae" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggae" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="56" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah

Short chords on the beats the bass leaves free: 2 and 4 in 4/4, 2 and 3 in a waltz. Goes with the Root and fifth bass line.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-oompah) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggae" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="56" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Every off-beat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Never on the beat: a short chord on every and. Count 1-AND-2-AND aloud, tap the beat with your foot and play only with the and. On guitar it is a chop, the chord choked right after it sounds.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggae" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="56" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}},{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 80 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggae" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggae" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggae" data-chart="C F|G C|Am F|G" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same comping rhythm in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Calypso**

### The pattern

A two-bar pattern. First bar (shown): beat 1, the and of 2 held, beat 3. Second bar: beat 2 and the and of 3.

It belongs in *Bossa nova*. Here it is in the bossa nova style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"compRhythm":"bossa"}}]'></div>

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-pad) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-charleston) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

**How to play it.** Two bars: beat 1, the and of 2 held, beat 3; then beat 2 and the and of 3. On guitar the thumb plays the bass on 1 and 3 while the fingers play this rhythm.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"compRhythm":"bossa"}},{"label":"Charleston (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Son montuno {#chords-montuno}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Son montuno**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar pattern of short chords. First bar (shown): 1, 2, the and of 2, the and of 3, the and of 4. Second bar: every off-beat. Here it is played as block chords, not the pianist's broken octaves.

It belongs in *Son montuno*. Here it is in the son montuno style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Son montuno","opts":{"compRhythm":"montuno"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Every off-beat

A short chord on the and of every beat and never on the beat: the ska and calypso afterbeat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-upbeats) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Son montuno, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars of short chords: 1, 2, the and of 2, the and of 3, the and of 4; then every off-beat. Keep it dry and even. The second bar is the off-beat chop you learned in the step before.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Son montuno","opts":{"compRhythm":"montuno"}},{"label":"Every off-beat (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 100 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Son montuno","opts":{"compRhythm":"montuno"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Son montuno","opts":{"compRhythm":"montuno"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C F|G7 C|C F|G7 C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Son montuno","opts":{"compRhythm":"montuno"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Quarter-note chords](chords.qmd#chords-quarters), [Every off-beat](chords.qmd#chords-upbeats).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Tumbao](bass.qmd#bass-tumbao) (bass line), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part), [Tumbao, two drums](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao2) (conga part), [Son clave (2-3)](drums.qmd#drums-clave) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in son montuno:** [Tumbao](bass.qmd#bass-tumbao) (bass line), [Son clave (2-3)](drums.qmd#drums-clave) (drum groove), [Tumbao, two drums](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao2) (conga part).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Latin group:** [Bossa nova](chords.qmd#chords-bossa), [Tango (habanera)](chords.qmd#chords-tango), [Cha-cha](chords.qmd#chords-chacha).

## Cha-cha {#chords-chacha}

*For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Cha-cha**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A chord on 2, then the cha-cha-cha: 3, the and of 3, and 4.

It belongs in *Cha-cha*. Here it is in the cha-cha style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"compRhythm":"chacha"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah

Short chords on the beats the bass leaves free: 2 and 4 in 4/4, 2 and 3 in a waltz. Goes with the Root and fifth bass line.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords.qmd#chords-oompah) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Cha-cha, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A chord on 2, then cha-cha-cha: 3, the and of 3, 4. Keep the three short and even.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"compRhythm":"chacha"}},{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"compRhythm":"chacha"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"compRhythm":"chacha"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am Dm|E7 Am|Dm E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"compRhythm":"chacha"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Quarter-note chords](chords.qmd#chords-quarters), [Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah](chords.qmd#chords-oompah).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Cha-cha](bass.qmd#bass-chacha) (bass line), [Cha-cha](drums.qmd#drums-chacha) (drum groove), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part).
- **Plays with, in cha-cha:** [Cha-cha](bass.qmd#bass-chacha) (bass line), [Cha-cha](drums.qmd#drums-chacha) (drum groove), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Latin group:** [Bossa nova](chords.qmd#chords-bossa), [Tango (habanera)](chords.qmd#chords-tango), [Son montuno](chords.qmd#chords-montuno).
